title: Washington School and schoolmate Bernard Hilda
summary: At Washington School he befriended Bernard Hilda, later a Paris impresario and bandleader, who recognised him decades later when Clarke came to Paris with Dizzy.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: I went to the Washington School with a lot of Jewish kids, and one of them is a friend of mine today. He's an impresario here in Paris, and we went to school, when we were about 12 or 13 years old, together.
Isn't that? Bernard Hildq. Have you ever heard of Bernard Hildq?
I think the name's familiar to me. Whom does he handle?
Oh, lots of acts. I don't remember now.
Oh, well, it doesn't matter. I just thought I'd ask.
But he had an orchestra at the time, and when I came to Paris with Dizzy and I stayed over and he

asked me to play with him. Now, we didn't recognize each other that time, because this was like '40, almost 30 years. So we began talking one day and he said, 'Little Kenny. Pittsburgh.' He said, 'I know a little Kenny from Pittsburgh, used to go to Washington School.' I said, 'Well, that's me.' He said, 'It can't be true.' And we found that we had been kids together.
: Isn't that funny. That is really very funny isn't it.
But he was a violinist, a very good violinist, who loved Rubinoff at the time. You know, he was a great fan of Rubinoff.
And I became attached to him because there was music, you know?
